title: Interactive Human-AI Alignment: Five Principles of SPEAR
description: A position paper reframing human-AI alignment as an ongoing interaction design problem, with five principles: Specification, Process, and Evaluation within a task, plus Adaptation and Recalibration across tasks and sessions.

title: DoubleAgents: Human-Agent Alignment in a Socially Embedded Workflow
authors: Tao Long*, Xuanming Zhang*, Sitong Wang, Zhou Yu, Lydia Chilton
description: DoubleAgents fosters human-AI alignment through distributed cognition by supporting exception handling, codifying reusable rules for agents, exposing transparent state tracking, and preserving user control over usages.

title: ParallelPilot: Supporting Coordination and Monitoring in Parallel AI Coding Workflows
authors: Tao Long, Weili Shi, Hussein Mozannar, Maya Murad, Rafah Hosn
description: As coding assistants become autonomous, developers run parallel sessions. We identified PILOT:  five supervisory practices as Planning, Isolating, Logging, Observing, and Triaging. We present ParallelPilot, an interface support increasing ticket throughput by 63% and perceived efficiency by 1.69 pts, while reducing tracking effort, context switching, and bookkeeping.

title: FeedQUAC: Quick Unobtrusive AI-Generated Commentary
authors: Tao Long, Kendra Wannamaker, Jo Vermeulen, George Fitzmaurice, Justin Matejka
description: FeedQUAC delivers ambient, read-aloud commentary from personas via shortcut keys and auditory cues.

title: Artistic Practice Opportunities in CST Evaluations: A Longitudinal Group Deployment of ArtKrit
authors: Catherine Liu*, Tao Long*, Asya Vaisberg, Chau Vu, Jiaju Ma, Jingyi Li
description: Deployed an artistic support tool for three weeks with designers embedded in 3 small, supportive artist networks.

title: From Planning to Revision: How AI Writing Support at Different Stages Alters Ownership
authors: Katy Gero, Tao Long, Carly Schnitzler, Paramveer Dhillon
description: A study with 253 participants shows that AI writing assistance reduces ownership overall, with the largest drop when AI supports drafting rather than planning or revising.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: What Might User-Centered Evaluation of Agentic AI Look Like?
description: A position paper argues that agentic AI evaluation should move beyond benchmarks to capture the lived, longitudinal dynamics of human-agent collaboration, including trust, delegation, and real user success.

title: Behind The Paper: A Workflow for Supporting Personal Research Reflection
authors: Tony Zhou, Tao Long, Ding Li, Gary Hsieh
description: An interview and corpus study (n=11 interviews; 15,749 reflections) presents a system that scaffolds research reflection without replacing author voice

title: Not Like Us, Hunty: Measuring Perceptions and Behavioral Effects of  Anthropomorphic Cues in LLMs
authors: Jeffrey Basoah, Daniel Chechelnitsky, Tao Long, Katharina Reinecke, Chrysoula Zerva, Kaitlyn Zhou, Mark Díaz, Maarten Sap
description: A study with 985 participants reveals sociolect-infused LLMs influence trust, reliance, and social presence.

title: Facilitating Longitudinal Interaction Studies of AI Systems
authors: Tao Long, Sitong Wang, Émilie Fabre, Tony Wang, Anup Sathya, Jason Wu, Savvas Dimitrios Petridis, Ding Li, David Ledo, Tuhin Chakrabarty, Yue Jiang, Jingyi Li, Tiffany Tseng, Ken Nakagaki, Qian Yang, Nikolas Martelaro,  Jeffrey Nickerson, Lydia Chilton
description: A workshop to facilitate discussion and advance research on long-term user studies in HCI.

title: Generative Disco: Text-to-Video for Music Visualization
authors: Vivian Liu, Tao Long, Jenny Ma, Nathan Raw, Lydia Chilton
description: Generates music videos from text prompts using LLMs and text-to-image models, with controllable transitions.

title: Not Just Novelty: A Longitudinal Study on Utility and Customization of an AI Workflow
authors: Tao Long, Katy Gero, Lydia Chilton
description: A 3-week longitudinal study showing a familiarization phase and increased AI usefulness through customization.

title: ReelFramer: Human-AI Co-Creation for News-to-Video Translation
authors: Sitong Wang, Samia Menon, Tao Long, Keren Henderson, Ding Li, Kevin Crowston, Mark Hansen, Jeffrey Nickerson, Lydia Chilton
description: ReelFramer supports news video generation through framings, storyboards, and scripts using LLMs.

title: Social Dynamics of AI Support in Creative Writing
authors: Katy Gero, Tao Long, Lydia Chilton
description: We identify social-technical gaps in AI-assisted writing, focused on motivation, planning, and user values.

title: Tweetorial Hooks: Generative AI Tools to Motivate Science on Social Media
authors: Tao Long, Dorothy Zhang, Grace Li, Batool Taraif, Samia Menon, Kynnedy Smith, Sitong Wang, Katy Gero, Lydia Chilton
description: HookIncubator helps STEM experts co-create compelling hooks for Twitter threads using LLM scaffolding.

title: Challenges and Opportunities for the Design of Smart Speakers
description: Identifies VUI design opportunities: multitasking, calm design, and mental models.

title: Audience Impressions of Narrative Structures and Personal Language Style in Science Communication
authors: Grace Li, Yuanyang Teng, Juna Kawai-Yue, Unaisah Ahmed, Anatta Tantiwongse, Jessica Y. Liang, Dorothy Zhang, Kynnedy Simone Smith, Tao Long, Mina Lee, Lydia Chilton
description: Social media techniques boost science engagement, but preferences and scientist comfort levels vary widely.

title: Perspectives from Participants and Researchers on Addressing Embodiment in a Virtual Cyberball Task
authors: Tao Long, Swati Pandita, Andrea Won
description: Discusses naive participants and researchers’ perspectives on designing inclusive VR studies.

title: Multi-stakeholder Perspectives on Digital Tools for U.S. Asylum Applicants Seeking Healthcare and Legal Information
authors: Aparajita Bhandari, Diana Freed, Tara Pilato, Faten Taki, Gunisha Kaur, Stephen Yale-Loehr, Jane Powers, Tao Long, Natalie Bazarova
description: Analyzes digital tool barriers for asylum applicants seeking healthcare/legal info.
